title: BirdCast forecast alerts underpin Houston's Lights Out Nights proclamation
summary: Houston Audubon issues Lights Out alerts from BirdCast forecasts; City of Houston proclaimed Lights Out Nights on 9 April 2021.
account: BirdCast is produced by the Cornell Lab of Ornithology with Colorado State University and now Purdue University and the University of Illinois. It forecasts nocturnal bird migration from a model trained on 23 years of weather-radar bird detections and reanalysis weather data. Houston Audubon states its staff use the BirdCast forecast maps to track migration predictions. They issue Lights Out Action Alerts when a chance of high migration coincides with weather events. Alerts ask residents and businesses to turn off nonessential lights from 11 p.m. to 6 a.m. during spring and fall migration. On 9 April 2021 the City of Houston proclaimed “Lights Out Nights” to help migrating birds. No Houston collision reduction is documented. A separate 21-year Chicago study co-authored by BirdCast scientists estimated halving lighted window area cuts collisions 11-fold in spring and 6-fold in fall.
purpose: Forecast nightly bird migration intensity from weather radar and weather models so that cities, building owners and residents can reduce lighting on high-migration nights.
system: BirdCast migration forecast model and Lights Out Action Alerts
developer: Cornell Lab of Ornithology, Colorado State University (forecasts now produced with Purdue University and University of Illinois)
deployer: Houston Audubon (Birds Houston) and City of Houston
segment: Migratory bird collision prevention / urban lighting policy

ratings.reason: Residents and building managers receive timed alerts, but no individual outcome is documented.
A municipal proclamation and partner alert program were adopted; the partner page reports no measured change in collisions at Houston buildings.
The collision evidence is a Chicago study co-authored by BirdCast scientists; Houston's own collision change is unmeasured.

ai_role.statement: The learned forecast model identifies the nights on which alerts are issued. The proclamation and alert program are documented by the operating partner, not the model's makers. The collision-reduction evidence comes from a separate Chicago study co-authored by BirdCast scientists and is not specific to Houston. The counterfactual for Houston is unproven.
